g.text: The long-run history of child mortality

text.style: font-size: 11.52px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #555555

g.text: Shown is the share of children who died before reaching the end of puberty. The age cut-off varies slightly between

text.style: font-size: 11.52px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #555555

g.text: studies, but is generally around 15 years.

text.style: font-size: 8.64px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: Note: Each pre-modern point is a single estimate for one population, drawn from 18 separate studies, and the periods they cover differ in length. The

text.style: font-size: 8.64px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: global series joins two sources: UN WPP for 1950-1989, UN IGME for 1990-2024. For 1990, the year both estimate, they differ by 0.2 percentage points.

text.style: font-size: 8.64px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #888888

g.text: Data source: Human Mortality Database (2025); Knodel (1970); UN IGME (2018; 2026); UN WPP (2024); Volk and Atkinson (2013)
